new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-13, Adams Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous resolution formalizing a June 22, 2026 motion to establish the moratorium (Butler County)
new_candidates.duration: 180 days from the July 13, 2026 resolution (following the June 22, 2026 motion) to draft a curative amendment addressing six business types not covered by current zoning: data centers, power generation plants, large-scale and accessory solar power systems, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, and dispensaries.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Adams Township Board of Supervisors resolution (a follow-up to the June 22, 2026 motion), invoking the municipal curative amendment process under the PA Municipalities Planning Code and declaring the zoning ordinance's exclusion of the six business types 'does not bear a substantial relationship to the public health, safety or morals' of residents, and that a sweeping ban 'cannot pass constitutional muster' and is therefore invalid (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: current zoning ordinance does not address data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, or dispensaries, allowing any of them to be built anywhere in the township. Board Chairman Russell Ford emphasized the action was preemptive, not prompted by any pending application.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 180-day expiry (~2027-01-09). Adopted via a unanimous June 22, 2026 motion and formalized by resolution at the July 13, 2026 meeting, the moratorium pauses applications for six business types (data centers, power generation plants, large-scale/accessory solar, last-mile fulfillment centers, micro-warehouses, dispensaries) while the township prepares a curative amendment to correct the declared invalidity. No news of an extension, adoption of the amendment, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; officials stated the moratorium was preemptive and not prompted by any pending application for any of the six covered business types.
new_candidates.outcome: Adams Township Board of Supervisors adopted a 180-day moratorium (via a June 22, 2026 motion, formalized by resolution on July 13, 2026) on six business types including data centers and large-scale solar, to allow time to draft a curative amendment to the zoning ordinance.

evidence.title: Adams Township passes data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the June 22, 2026 unanimous vote approving a 180-day moratorium on applications for data centers and five other business types, and that officials described it as a preemptive measure.
evidence.quote: The Adams Township Board of Supervisors approved a 180-day moratorium on applications for six types of businesses, including data centers, at its regular meeting Monday, June 22.

evidence.title: Adams Twp. takes the next step toward data center amendment
evidence.supports: Confirms the July 13, 2026 formal resolution, quotes its findings of invalidity, and states it was a follow-up to the June 22 motion.
evidence.quote: The resolution was a follow-up to a motion made at the June 22 meeting to establish a moratorium and allows the township up to 180 days to draft a "curative amendment" to the township's zoning ordinance.

new_candidates.notes: No township-hosted resolution PDF was located; relying on two Butler Eagle articles covering the June 22 motion and the July 13 follow-up resolution. This is a separate instrument from the neighboring, already-tracked pa-center-township-2026 row, which the July 31, 2026 Butler Eagle countywide roundup names alongside Adams Township as having 'enacted 180-day moratoriums.'

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-05-18, Mount Carmel Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote (Northumberland County)
new_candidates.duration: 180 days from May 18, 2026 to complete a municipal curative amendment ('Zoning Amendment') addressing data centers.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Mount Carmel Township municipal curative amendment under the PA Municipalities Planning Code; the township's own site describes it simply as the '180 day moratorium enacted on May 18, 2026,' the end result of which will be a curative amendment to correct zoning invalidities regarding data centers (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with sustained community opposition: hundreds of residents packed public meetings (including a May 13, 2026 hearing) opposing data-center development in the township; officials say they cannot outright ban the use but are working to limit and define it through zoning.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, nearing its computed 2026-11-14 end date. The township presented an ordinance work-progress update on July 15, 2026 and a preliminary draft ordinance update on Aug. 12, 2026; a public hearing for comment only (no board vote that night) was advertised for Sept. 23, 2026 at Mount Carmel Area High School. No news of an extension, adoption of the final ordinance, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named as pending at adoption; the moratorium responded to general community opposition and rumors of data-center interest in the township rather than a specific filed application.
new_candidates.outcome: Mount Carmel Township Board of Supervisors adopted a 180-day moratorium on data-center proposals on 2026-05-18 to allow time to draft a curative-amendment zoning ordinance, with a public-comment hearing on the draft ordinance held Sept. 23, 2026.

evidence.title: Mount Carmel Township - Zoning Amendment Update
evidence.supports: Official township homepage confirming the 180-day moratorium enacted May 18, 2026, the Sept. 23, 2026 public-comment hearing, and the Aug. 12, 2026 preliminary draft ordinance presentation.
evidence.quote: The Township is currently under a 180 day moratorium enacted on May 18, 2026. The end result will be a municipal curative amendment to correct zoning invalidities and regulation with regard to data centers.

evidence.title: Hundreds in Mt. Carmel Township speak out in opposition to data center development
evidence.supports: Confirms strong community opposition and township supervisors' statements that they cannot outright ban data centers but are working on zoning to limit development.
evidence.quote: While the township supervisors say they cannot outright ban data center development, they invited folks in and around the township to talk about a new zoning ordinance that would limit data center development.

new_candidates.notes: Also referred to as 'Carmel Township' in some secondary sources; the township's own name and web domain (mctownship.org) confirm 'Mount Carmel Township' as the correct jurisdiction name. The associated newsitem.com articles were blocked by a cookie/subscription wall in this pass; the official township site and WNEP corroborate the same facts.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-06-16, Doylestown Township Board of Supervisors vote (Bucks County)
new_candidates.duration: 180 days (six months) from June 16, 2026 to adopt new data-center zoning rules; during that time no data-center application may be submitted or reviewed in the township.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Doylestown Township Board of Supervisors resolution (adopted June 16, 2026) invoking the municipal curative amendment process, declaring the zoning ordinance's failure to identify or regulate data centers 'substantively invalid' (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed); township solicitor Peter Nelson advised the process requires adoption of a new ordinance within 180 days and bars reuse of the same curative-amendment tool for three years.
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance does not identify or regulate data centers as a permitted use; adopted proactively as part of a broader wave of Bucks County municipalities (following neighboring Falls Township's contested Amazon data center) acting to define and regulate the use before an application arrives.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, nearing its computed 2026-12-13 end date. The vote does not itself adopt final zoning rules; it starts a 180-day period for officials and consultants to draft standards on where data centers may be located, how they are defined, and what development standards would apply. No application is pending in the township.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None; no data center application is pending in Doylestown Township.
new_candidates.outcome: Doylestown Township Board of Supervisors voted on June 16, 2026 to begin a 180-day municipal curative amendment process, temporarily freezing any data-center applications while the township drafts zoning rules.

evidence.title: Doylestown Township moves to block data center applications while crafting zoning rules
evidence.supports: Detailed account of the June 16, 2026 vote, direct quotes from Township Solicitor Peter Nelson on the 180-day curative amendment mechanism, and confirmation that no data-center application can be submitted or reviewed during the period.
evidence.quote: Doylestown Township supervisors voted last week to begin a 180-day curative amendment process aimed at regulating data centers, temporarily freezing any such applications while township officials draft zoning rules for the increasingly scrutinized land use.

new_candidates.notes: A companion Bucks County Herald article (buckscountyherald.com) corroborates the same action but was behind a subscriber wall in this pass and could not be read beyond its headline/teaser; relying on the single detailed Bucks Independence account.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-27, Falls Township Board of Supervisors vote (Bucks County)
new_candidates.duration: 180 days from July 27, 2026 for the township to review and potentially amend Chapter 209 of its zoning ordinance regarding data centers.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Falls Township Board of Supervisors resolution (adopted July 27, 2026) declaring a portion of the zoning ordinance 'substantively invalid' as to data centers, initiating a municipal curative amendment as a 'protective measure' against substantive-validity challenges (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with sustained public opposition to the already-approved Amazon Web Services data center (a 2-million-square-foot, 10-building campus under construction at the former U.S. Steel/Keystone Trade Center site); residents demanded clearer definitions of 'data center' and infrastructure/utility standards for future proposals.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 2027-01-23 end date. The curative amendment does not affect the already-approved (March 2025) Amazon Web Services data center, which remains under construction; township staff will review the existing zoning ordinance and bring proposed amendments back to the Board within 180 days, with drafts to be posted publicly and advertised before hearings.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None going forward; the curative amendment explicitly does not affect the already-approved and under-construction Amazon Web Services data center at the former U.S. Steel site, whose approval (March 2025) and community pushback prompted this action.
new_candidates.outcome: Falls Township Board of Supervisors voted July 27, 2026 to declare part of its zoning ordinance substantively invalid as to data centers, opening a 180-day curative-amendment period to draft new zoning rules.

evidence.title: Falls to Examine Zoning Ordinance in Response to Data Center Opposition
evidence.supports: Official township news post confirming the Monday (July 27, 2026) vote, the 180-day review period, and that the curative amendment has no impact on the already-approved Amazon data center.
evidence.quote: Following a widely attended and contentious community meeting for the Amazon data center in Falls Township, the Supervisors on Monday approved a resolution declaring a portion of the zoning ordinance ‘substantively invalid.’

evidence.title: Falls Twp. Declares Part Of Zoning Ordinance 'Invalid' After Data Center Outcry
evidence.supports: Independent, detailed account of the same July 27, 2026 vote, including township solicitor and supervisor quotes and the Amazon data center's water/power details.
evidence.quote: The Falls Township Board of Supervisors voted Monday to declare portions of the municipality's zoning ordinance “substantively invalid.”

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-07, Conewago Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote adopting Resolution 2026-13 (York County)
new_candidates.duration: 180-day moratorium on all data center applications, per the township's own presentation materials.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution 2026-13 (Conewago Township, York County), adopted unanimously at the July 7, 2026 Board of Supervisors meeting, invoking the municipal curative-amendment process to prevent a developer from filing a substantive validity challenge to the township's zoning ordinance over its silence on data centers.
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: zoning ordinance did not address data centers; a draft data-center ordinance and zoning overlay map, developed with township counsel (Eckert Seamans) and engineering consultant (CS Davidson), was presented to the public at a July 23, 2026 special joint meeting of the Board of Supervisors and Planning Commission.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its official 2027-01-03 end date (per the township's own presentation). A draft ordinance establishing a Data Center Overlay district (100-acre minimum parcel, 250-foot perimeter setback, 90-foot height cap, 50-foot landscaped buffer, acoustic standards, etc.) has been presented publicly but not yet adopted as of this research pass; residents continue to organize opposition to rezoning for data centers in the township.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; a prior 2025 proposal to rezone land near Bible Baptist Church for a data center (developer identified in some coverage) drew opposition but is treated separately from this proactive, township-wide moratorium.
new_candidates.outcome: Conewago Township Board of Supervisors unanimously adopted Resolution 2026-13 on 2026-07-07, a 180-day moratorium on data-center applications (ending 2027-01-03), while it develops a Data Center Overlay zoning ordinance.

evidence.title: Conewago Township Special Joint Meeting Presentation: DRAFT Data Center Ordinance and Overlay Map
evidence.supports: Official township presentation confirming Resolution 2026-13 was adopted unanimously at the July 7, 2026 Board of Supervisors meeting, that it imposes a 180-day moratorium on all data center applications, that it prevents substantive-validity challenges, and that the moratorium ends January 3, 2027; also details the draft Data Center Overlay ordinance's standards.
evidence.quote: At the July 7, 2026 Board of Supervisor's meeting, the Supervisors unanimously voted to adopt Resolution 2026-13. This Resolution puts in place a 180 day moratorium on all applications for data center... The 180 day moratorium ends on January 3, 2027

new_candidates.notes: A Civic IQ aggregator page surfaced a claim of a further extension via 'Resolution 2026-19' (Aug. 11, 2026, 'extend the commercial data center moratorium for 180 days'); on inspection, that Civic IQ page's actual agency tag is 'Town of York charter, Michigan' (a generic template page, not Conewago Township, PA) -- the same misattribution pattern found and disregarded for pa-warrington-township-2026 in the prior research pass -- so it is disregarded here as unreliable rather than reported as a status change.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-09, Williamsport City Council, 6-0 vote adopting Resolution #10088 (Lycoming County)
new_candidates.duration: 180 days from adoption to enact a curative amendment under 53 P.S. Section 10609.2, with a follow-up resolution required within 30 days making specific findings of invalidity. Councilman Milliken characterized it as effectively 'hitting pause' on data-center development even though the resolution does not describe itself as a 'pause.'
new_candidates.legal_basis: Resolution #10088 (City of Williamsport), adopted 6-0 by City Council on July 9, 2026, declaring the city's Zoning Ordinance (enacted April 16, 1998, amended since) substantively invalid insofar as it excludes data centers and ancillary buildings or uses, including but not limited to power generating facilities, and proposing preparation of a curative amendment under 53 P.S. Section 10609.2; a follow-up Resolution #10091 was required within 30 days to make specific findings of the declared invalidity.
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: 1998 zoning ordinance does not account for data centers or their accessory uses; adopted proactively, following similar curative-amendment action by Lycoming County and several county townships, to close the loophole that would otherwise let a developer file a landowner curative amendment and force approval of a data center anywhere in the city.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 2027-01-05 end date. No data center is presently planned in the City of Williamsport; the resolution was the city's opening move in a regional contest over who regulates data-center siting, alongside Lycoming County's own curative amendment (pa-lycoming-county-2026, a separate, already-tracked instrument covering the county's 19 zoning-partner municipalities, which does not include the City of Williamsport).
new_candidates.affected_projects: None; no data center application is pending in the City of Williamsport as of adoption.
new_candidates.outcome: Williamsport City Council adopted Resolution #10088 on 2026-07-09, a 6-0 vote declaring the city's zoning ordinance substantively invalid as to data centers and opening a 180-day curative-amendment period.

evidence.title: Resolution #10088 (City of Williamsport)
evidence.supports: Primary text of the resolution declaring the zoning ordinance substantively invalid as to data centers and ancillary power-generating facilities, and proposing a curative amendment within 180 days plus specific findings within 30 days.
evidence.quote: Pursuant to the powers vested in it by 53 P.S. §10609.2, the Council of the City of Williamsport proposes to prepare a curative amendment to validate, or reaffirm the validity of, its zoning ordinance, and to enact same within one hundred eighty (180) days of the date of adoption of this Resolution.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-07-14, Little Britain Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote adopting the formal moratorium resolution (Lancaster County); preceded by a June 9, 2026 preliminary vote to move forward with the same moratorium concept.
new_candidates.duration: 180 days from the July 14, 2026 resolution, preventing submission of any applications for data centers, their ancillary structures, or energy generation, while the township develops a zoning ordinance.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Little Britain Township Board of Supervisors resolution (adopted July 14, 2026) declaring existing ordinances invalid regarding data centers and related uses because they are not addressed, initiating a municipal curative amendment (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap: the township has no ordinance specifically addressing data centers; adopted proactively while the board develops a new ordinance modeled on those of nearby townships.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23, running toward its computed 2027-01-10 end date. No news of an extension, adoption of the amendment, or repeal was found in sources reviewed through 2026-09-23.
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named; adopted proactively rather than in response to a pending application.
new_candidates.outcome: Little Britain Township Board of Supervisors unanimously adopted a resolution on 2026-07-14 imposing a 180-day moratorium on data-center applications, following a preliminary June 9, 2026 vote to move forward with the concept.

evidence.title: Little Britain Township board passes resolution to pause development of new data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the July 14, 2026 unanimous vote adopting the formal resolution, that it declares existing ordinances invalid regarding data centers, and that it bars applications for data centers, ancillary structures, or energy generation for 180 days.

evidence.quote: The board voted to move forward with placing a 180-day moratorium on data center applications while they work on an ordinance to address these proposals.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2026-04-30, Clinton Township Board of Supervisors vote to put a six-month moratorium in place while reviewing a draft data-center ordinance (Wayne County); exact duration in calendar days not confirmed in sources reviewed.
new_candidates.duration: Approximately six months (treated here as 180 days) from the April 30, 2026 vote, to allow the township and Wayne County Planning Commissions to review a draft data-center/SALDO ordinance before adoption.
new_candidates.legal_basis: Clinton Township Board of Supervisors vote (April 30, 2026 meeting) adopting a six-month moratorium on data-center applications while a draft Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance (SALDO) amendment, prepared by Solicitor Jeffrey Treat since a December 2025 request, is reviewed by the Township and Wayne County Planning Commissions (specific resolution number not located in sources reviewed).
new_candidates.trigger: Specific project combined with a regulatory gap: the moratorium was adopted the same day Linde Corporation submitted a proposal for a data center and gas-fired power plants on a 758-acre former mining parcel near Browndale, on land identified as containing one of only two 'exceptional value waters' streams in Wayne County (Roger's Creek, tributary to the Lackawanna/Susquehanna); the township had already been drafting data-center standards since a December 2025 board request.
new_candidates.current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23; the moratorium's precise end date is not independently confirmed (estimated late October 2026 from a six-month term starting April 30, 2026). Since adoption, Linde Corporation's application (submitted the same day as the moratorium) proceeded through contested public hearings, including a May 7, 2026 planning commission session drawing roughly 250 attendees. On 2026-09-14, the Board of Supervisors -- following a unanimous Planning Commission recommendation to deny -- unanimously rejected Linde's preliminary land development plan for 20 data center buildings and two gas-fired power plants, finding it did not meet the township's Subdivision and Land Development Ordinance (insufficient detail on environmental protections, stormwater management, and infrastructure impacts). Linde is widely expected to appeal to Wayne County Court.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Linde Corporation's proposed $6 billion data center and two gas-fired power plants on 758 acres of former mining land near Browndale; the application was submitted April 30, 2026 (the same day the moratorium was adopted) and was unanimously rejected by the Board of Supervisors on 2026-09-14 for failing to meet SALDO standards; an appeal to Wayne County Court is expected.
new_candidates.outcome: Clinton Township (Wayne County) Board of Supervisors voted on 2026-04-30 to impose a six-month moratorium on data-center applications while it finalized a data-center ordinance; the township separately and unanimously rejected the pending Linde Corporation data center/power-plant land development plan on 2026-09-14 for failing to meet subdivision and land development standards.

evidence.title: 'We don't want you here': Clinton Township hears resident input on data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the April 30, 2026 board vote to send the draft ordinance to the planning commission and to put a six-month moratorium in place, that Linde's application was submitted the same day, and details on the draft ordinance's 1,000-foot buffer and water-study requirements.
evidence.quote: At its meeting of Thursday, April 30, the board voted to send a draft ordinance to the planning commission for review, and to put a six-month moratorium in place, to give the township time to review and adopt that ordinance.

evidence.title: Clinton Township Rejects Proposed $6 Billion Linde Data Center Project
evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 14, 2026 (Wednesday night) unanimous Board of Supervisors vote rejecting Linde's application on SALDO-compliance grounds, following a Planning Commission recommendation to deny, and that an appeal to Wayne County Court is expected.
evidence.quote: Opponents of data center expansion in Northeast Pennsylvania scored a key victory Wednesday night after Clinton Township officials voted unanimously to reject a proposed $6 billion data center development submitted by Linde Corporation.

new_candidates.notes: Exact duration in days (as opposed to 'six months') and any formal resolution/ordinance number were not located in sources reviewed; the six-month figure is used to compute an approximate 2026-10-27 end date. This entry is distinct from Linde's separate, subsequently rejected land development application, which is recorded as an affected project rather than a separate moratorium.

new_candidates.date_enacted: 2025-08-11, Dorrance Township Board of Supervisors, unanimous vote (Luzerne County)
new_candidates.duration: Up to 180 days from Aug. 11, 2025 to amend the zoning ordinance; the process concluded early when the township adopted a permanent zoning amendment on 2025-09-22 (about six weeks later).
new_candidates.legal_basis: Dorrance Township Board of Supervisors ordinance (adopted 2025-08-11) imposing 'a temporary moratorium of the acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for data centers and similar technology, related businesses that consume large amounts of power and use water for cooling, throughout all zoning districts of the township'; superseded by a permanent zoning amendment adopted 2025-09-22 (unanimous 3-0 vote) establishing conditional-use standards for data centers, data center accessory structures, power substations, and data center campuses.
new_candidates.trigger: Regulatory gap combined with public pressure: zoning ordinance was silent on data centers; adopted after more than 100 residents packed a planning commission meeting following rumors that a data center was planned for the township, though officials said no proposal had been received.
new_candidates.current_status: Replaced as of 2025-09-22. The township's Aug. 11, 2025 temporary moratorium was superseded about six weeks later when supervisors voted 3-0 to permanently amend the zoning ordinance's conditional-use standards to regulate data centers, data center accessory structures, power substations, and data center campuses (covering noise, vibration, traffic and police/fire impact, and a water feasibility study requirement). The permanent amendment was later challenged by developer Brewster Land Company (landowner curative amendment / validity challenge over a 155-acre B-2-zoned parcel); the Zoning Hearing Board rejected that challenge (outcome reported as a township 'win' around 2026-05/06), and the developer has since appealed to court (as of an Aug. 31, 2026 report).
new_candidates.affected_projects: None named as pending at the original moratorium's adoption. The subsequent zoning-validity challenge came from Brewster Land Company over a 155-acre B-2 parcel, adjudicated separately by the Zoning Hearing Board and later appealed to court by the developer.
new_candidates.outcome: Dorrance Township Board of Supervisors adopted a temporary moratorium on data-center applications on 2025-08-11, which was replaced about six weeks later by a permanent zoning amendment (2025-09-22) establishing conditional-use standards for data centers, data center accessory structures, power substations, and data center campuses.

evidence.title: Dorrance Twp. supervisors look at blocking data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the Aug. 11, 2025 unanimous vote adopting a temporary moratorium ordinance on data-center applications across all zoning districts, and that no proposal had actually been received.
evidence.quote: Supervisors voted unanimously to approve an ordinance imposing a temporary moratorium of the “acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for data centers and similar technology, related businesses that consume large amounts of power and use water for cooling, throughout all zoning districts of the township.”

evidence.title: Dorrance Twp. amends zoning ordinance to address data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the Sept. 22, 2025 unanimous 3-0 vote adopting the permanent conditional-use zoning amendment for data centers, data center accessory structures, power substations, and data center campuses, superseding the original moratorium.
evidence.quote: Dorrance Twp. supervisors voted to amend the township's code of ordinances regarding data centers at a public hearing Monday morning. The unanimous 3-0 vote was in regard to amendments provided by township solicitor Sean Logsdon that dealt with regulations having to do with data centers, data center accessory structures, power substations and data center campuses within the township.

new_candidates.notes: Predates the roughly 2026-08-01 discovery window but is an older instrument the inventory missed; savrn.com's tracker lists this jurisdiction with a 'Validation 2026-06-19' note that the subsequent Brewster Land Company zoning-validity challenge (a separate, later dispute over the permanent amendment, not the original moratorium) was resolved in the township's favor.
